nodes.description: Isoniazid, rifampicin and pyrazinamide are hepatotoxic, and drug-induced liver injury is the commonest serious adverse effect of standard therapy, reported in 2 to 28% of treated tuberculosis patients. Pre-existing liver disease is a risk factor, and in hepatic tuberculosis the injury is hard to tell apart from the disease itself or, in people starting antiretroviral therapy, from hepatic immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome. In one 14-patient hepatobiliary series, treatment adverse effects, mainly drug-induced hepatitis, occurred in 42.9%.

nodes.description: Four-drug therapy with isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol for two months, then isoniazid and rifampicin, for a total of 6 to 12 months, as for other extrapulmonary sites. Regimens containing isoniazid and rifampicin lowered mortality compared with monotherapy. Caveat: isoniazid, rifampicin and pyrazinamide are hepatotoxic, pre-existing liver disease raises the risk, and drug-induced liver injury is hard to separate from hepatic tuberculosis itself or from immune reconstitution in HIV. ALT should be monitored in patients with liver disease or HIV, and treatment interrupted and a modified regimen used if ALT exceeds three times the upper limit of normal with symptoms or jaundice, or five times without.
